Hong Kong Reels as Typhoon Haishen Brings Widespread Disruption

Hong Kong is experiencing severe disruption across the city as Typhoon Haishen continues to batter the territory with torrential rain and gale-force winds, prompting the Hong Kong Observatory to maintain the No. 10 hurricane signal for a second consecutive day. The typhoon, one of the strongest in recent years, has brought citywide flooding, halted transport, and caused widespread power outages, raising concerns over economic losses that could stretch into billions of Hong Kong dollars.

Major roads across Kowloon and Hong Kong Island are submerged, with flash floods reported in low-lying districts such as Sham Shui Po and Chai Wan. The Mass Transit Railway (MTR) has suspended above-ground services, and the Airport Authority confirmed that all flights are grounded until further notice. The Hong Kong Port and Maritime Board announced that all container terminals have ceased operations, delaying hundreds of shipments.

“Given the scale of this event, we expect significant short-term impacts on logistics, retail, and financial services,” said Irene Chiu, chief economist at the Hong Kong Economic Forum. “The city’s interconnected infrastructure means the effects are being felt across every sector.”

The Education Bureau has ordered the closure of all schools, while the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce urged employers to implement remote working arrangements where possible. “Employee safety is paramount, but the economic cost will be substantial,” said chamber chair Victor Yuen.

More than 200 people have been injured, and the Hospital Authority is urging residents to avoid unnecessary travel. Emergency crews are working around the clock to clear fallen trees and restore power, but authorities warn that with Haishen forecast to linger over the region for another 24 hours, further disruptions are likely.

“The economic impact will depend on how quickly essential services can be restored,” said Clara Wong, an analyst at Lotus Advisory. “For now, the priority is public safety.”
